title: November 2 pre-market: EchoStar deal talks and a Coherent upgrade lift shares
summary: EchoStar advances on reported SpaceX talks and Coherent gains after an upgrade. Fox subsequently reports stronger advertising and profit; manufacturing data is the next test.

sections.text:
EchoStar rose 6.69% to $103.43 before open. A November 2 report said SpaceX was in talks to buy Boost Mobile or use its network, citing the Washington Post. The companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment in that report. No signed transaction has been announced.

The investment question is how any agreement would alter EchoStar’s cash needs and continuing responsibilities. Selling a business and selling access to a network have different effects on revenue, costs and future investment. Price, retained obligations and required consents will determine whether a transaction improves the balance sheet and cash flow.
sections.heading: 1) EchoStar: reported Boost talks put the business mix in focus

sections.text:
Coherent rose 6.60% to $224.20 after Northland analyst Tim Savageaux upgraded it to Outperform on November 2. This is a fresh positive analyst assessment ahead of the company’s confirmed November 4 report after close.

Coherent supplies optical components, lasers and materials. Datacenters and communications accounted for about 74% of fiscal 2026 revenue, making demand from AI infrastructure especially important. Its August outlook called for September-quarter revenue of $2.2–$2.4 billion and adjusted profit per share of $1.85–$2.05. Investors should look for production expansion that supports growth while protecting margins.
sections.heading: 2) Coherent: an upgrade ahead of the next earnings test

sections.text:
Fox’s earlier pre-market price comparison was $66.81, up 5.65%, before its earnings release. The company subsequently reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 results for the three months ended September 30. The earlier price move should therefore be read separately from these newly released results.

Revenue was $4.571 billion, with reported profit per share of $2.20 and adjusted profit per share of $2.54. Adjusted profit excludes specified costs. Advertising revenue increased 47%, supported by the World Cup, political advertising and digital growth led by Tubi. Higher sports and digital-content costs partly offset the sales improvement.

The October ISM manufacturing survey is due during trading on November 2. Stronger orders can support industrial suppliers’ sales outlook, while input-cost pressure can limit the benefit to profits.
sections.heading: 3) Fox results strengthen the advertising picture

sections.text:
Xcel Energy’s October 29 earnings release provides recent context for the utility watchlist. It reported third-quarter GAAP and ongoing profit per share of $1.52, narrowed its 2026 ongoing outlook to $4.10–$4.16 and issued a 2027 range of $4.48–$4.62. These are previously reported results, not a new Monday announcement.

For the morning’s highlighted stories, watch for concrete deal terms at EchoStar, the coming earnings evidence at Coherent and the durability of Fox’s advertising growth, and the balance between orders and input costs in the manufacturing survey. Thin pre-market trading and new information can produce sharp reversals.

title: Nvidia slides after its board opens a probe as U.S. stocks rise before the November 9 open
summary: Nvidia fell nearly 6% before the November 9 open after its board announced an independent investigation. AMD and power producers gained as investors looked ahead to earnings and Tuesday’s inflation report.

sections.heading: 1) Why Nvidia stood out
sections.text: Nvidia’s board announced on November 8 that independent directors would investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. Its November 3 report showed $8.5 billion in quarterly data-center sales, up 97% from a year earlier.

title: CoreWeave earnings revive AI demand hopes before the open — November 11, 2026
summary: CoreWeave jumps 16.95% after stronger revenue and a higher outlook. Nebius earnings are the next AI cloud test, while inflation and financing costs remain risks.

sections.heading: 1) AI demand brings buyers back
sections.text:
November 11, 2026 · Before open. Moves are versus the previous regular close.

CoreWeave gained 16.95% after its November 10 earnings release, helping revive confidence in AI infrastructure spending. QQQ rose 1.88% and SPY gained 0.86%, showing stronger demand for technology shares than for the broader market.

sections.heading: 2) CoreWeave grows, but funding still matters
sections.text:
For the quarter ended September 30, CoreWeave reported revenue of $3.661 billion and raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $13.0–$13.3 billion. That strengthens the case that demand for rented AI computing is turning into sales.

The company still lost $709 million under standard accounting rules. Its $37–$39 billion capital-spending outlook shows how much investment is required before that growth can reward shareholders.

sections.heading: 3) Nebius is the next company-specific test
sections.text: Nebius rose 14.40%. It has confirmed third-quarter results for November 12 before the open. Investors can compare revenue growth, capacity expansion and funding needs with CoreWeave’s report; that comparison will show whether sector optimism is supported by Nebius’s own progress.

sections.heading: 5) The next decisions to watch
sections.text:
MSCI plans to announce index changes after the close on November 11, with implementation at the November 30 close. Inclusion can attract purchases by index-tracking funds, while removal can create selling pressure; the actual lists matter.

Producer-price inflation is scheduled for November 13 before the open. Stronger inflation could keep borrowing costs high, a particular challenge for companies building expensive data centers.

title: Nvidia leadership uncertainty weighs on AI stocks as Lilly gains — November 12, 2026
summary: Nvidia falls 7.64% before the open as reports of a possible leadership change unsettle AI stocks. Lilly gains after China approves its weight-loss pill; AMD also rises.

sections.heading: 1) Leadership risk weighs on technology
sections.text:
November 12, 2026 · Before open. Moves are versus the previous regular close.

Nvidia fell 7.64% as reports that its board was considering replacing CEO Jensen Huang unsettled investors. A leadership change had not been officially confirmed in the reporting reviewed. CoreWeave fell 5.55%, while QQQ and SPY declined 0.69% and 0.36%.

The investment issue is continuity at a central supplier to the AI industry. Leadership uncertainty can affect what investors are willing to pay for future growth, even before it changes sales.

sections.heading: 2) AMD gains as investors weigh alternatives
sections.text:
AMD rose 2.75%. William Blair upgraded it to Outperform, a positive analyst rating, and pointed to opportunities while Nvidia faces leadership uncertainty.

Winning more customers could lift AMD’s revenue. That remains an opportunity rather than a confirmed transfer of Nvidia business; product performance, availability and customer adoption will determine the outcome.

sections.heading: 3) Lilly gets a new market opening
sections.text:
Eli Lilly gained 2.87% after China approved orforglipron, its oral weight-loss medicine. Pills could attract patients who prefer not to use injections, expanding the potential customer base.

Approval allows market entry, but sales will depend on pricing, access and competition. It does not guarantee a particular revenue increase.

sections.heading: 4) Nebius and inflation are the next tests
sections.text:
Nebius rose 2.45%. The company scheduled third-quarter results for November 12 before the open and an earnings discussion that morning. Investors should watch sales growth, capacity additions and financing needs. Its reporting schedule is an upcoming decision point, not evidence of an earnings beat.

The October Producer Price Index, which measures prices received by producers, is scheduled for November 13 before the open. Persistent inflation could keep borrowing expensive and pressure the value investors place on future profits.

title: Weekly market recap · October 19–23, 2026
summary: The main takeaway: this was a mixed week, with smaller companies holding up better than major technology shares. Next, watch whether earnings outlooks and the Fed’s message support that broader strength.

sections.heading: The week in markets
sections.text: Big U.S. stocks ended the week slightly lower: the S&P 500 fell 0.47%, while the Nasdaq-100 fund QQQ lost 0.76%. Weakness in some of the largest technology companies weighed on the main indexes.

sections.heading: Where stocks showed strength
sections.text: The picture was stronger beneath the headline indexes. More stocks rose than fell, and the Russell 2000 index of smaller companies gained about 2%, showing that the week’s weakness was not shared across the market.

sections.heading: Weekly stock movers
sections.text: Hasbro led the weekly gainers with an 18.91% rise, followed by Charles River Laboratories at 15.07%. The heatmap also shows strength in Roper Technologies and Allegion.

sections.heading: Weekly stock movers
sections.text: Comfort Systems fell 19.33% and Howmet Aerospace lost 15.86%, among the week’s steepest declines. Construction-related companies were a weak spot, while several large technology stocks also finished lower.

sections.heading: Earnings in focus
sections.text: Meta reported profits and sales above expectations, while Tesla’s profits beat estimates and sales were roughly in line. Better-than-expected results do not always lead to a rising share price; investors also weigh the outlook.

sections.heading: Other market moves
sections.text: Gold fell about 4.1% over the week, while U.S. crude oil gained about 2%. These moves can affect mining and energy companies differently from the broader stock market.

sections.heading: The week ahead
sections.text: Next week brings the Fed’s October 28 rate decision and a busy earnings calendar. Microsoft and Alphabet are expected to report on October 28, followed by Amazon on October 29; dates can change.
